literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 尽管有先进的监测,疫情仍迅速加剧,并给初级医疗系统带来巨大压力。 [10.1186/s13690-026-02119-3]
在虫媒病毒中鉴定出 基孔肯雅病毒,登革热病毒血清型 1、2、4、寨卡病毒和 基孔肯雅病毒 的总体阳性率为 30.76%。 [PMCID:PMC13674194]
疫苗 和感染诱导的抗体对两种 CHIKV 基因型提供了强大的保护,即使浓度接近 ELISA 检测限。针对 MAYV 的防护需要更高的抗体滴度。 [10.1038/s41541-026-01604-8]
该研究报告称,CHIK-LA 已失去美国批准,并且缺乏关于人类 疫苗 对任一 疫苗 功效的充分数据。它还强调了 CHIK-LA 早期安全信号的存在,表明缺少可靠的人类安全数据集。 [10.1093/infdis/jiag284]

在 1023 名学生中,有 119 名做出回应 (11.6%),其中临床前学生所占比例过高 (p<0.001)。平均知识为 5.43/9,蚊子生物学知识(72.5%)强于病毒知识(54.2%)。中位严重度为 6.00/7,而易感性为 4.25/7。知识因研究阶段而异(p<0.001),与严重程度相关(rs = 0.399),但与易感性无关。 [10.64898/2026.10.15.26365696]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The epidemic accelerated rapidly despite advanced surveillance, placing substantial pressure on primary care systems. [10.1186/s13690-026-02119-3]
Chikungunya virus was identified among the arboviruses, with an overall positivity rate of 30.76% for Dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, and 4, Zika virus, and Chikungunya virus. [PMCID:PMC13674194]

Vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies provided strong protection against both CHIKV genotypes, even at concentrations close to ELISA detection limits. Protection against MAYV required higher antibody titers. [10.1038/s41541-026-01604-8]

The study found that the median age of patients was 69 years, with 91% having at least one comorbidity. The main organ failures were renal (59%), circulatory (43%), respiratory (41%), and neurological (14%). [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11123137/v1]

The study reports that CHIK-LA has lost its US approval and that adequate data on human vaccine efficacy for either vaccine is lacking. It also highlights the presence of early safety signals for CHIK-LA, indicating a robust human safety dataset is missing. [10.1093/infdis/jiag284]

papers.title: What a highly monitored chikungunya epidemic reveals about preparedness for Europe and beyond.
papers.abstract: The 2024-25 chikungunya epidemic in Reunion Island illustrates the challenge of translating early warning into timely public-health action during fast-moving arboviral outbreaks. Despite advanced surveillance, the epidemic accelerated rapidly and placed substantial pressure on primary care. These challenges, together with the complexity of emergency vaccine deployment, highlight the need for anticipatory, integrated preparedness strategies combining surveillance, vaccination, vector control and research.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2024-25 chikungunya epidemic in Reunion Island illustrates the challenge of translating early warning into timely public-health action during fast-moving arboviral outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed the 2024-25 chikungunya epidemic in Reunion Island, focusing on the challenges faced during the outbreak and the impact on public health systems.
analysis.methods: The study relied on surveillance data and reports from public health authorities to assess the challenges and pressures on healthcare systems during the epidemic.
analysis.main_results: The epidemic accelerated rapidly despite advanced surveillance, placing substantial pressure on primary care systems.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The challenges observed during the epidemic highlight the need for anticipatory, integrated preparedness strategies that combine surveillance, vaccination, vector control and research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of integrated preparedness strategies for managing future chikungunya outbreaks, particularly in regions with similar epidemiological profiles.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on observational data and does not include detailed statistical analysis or experimental methods, which limits the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the 2024-25 chikungunya epidemic in Reunion Island, highlighting the difficulties in translating early warning signals into effective public health responses during fast-moving outbreaks. The research underscores the challenges faced by primary care systems and emphasizes the need for integrated preparedness strategies that include surveillance, vaccination, vector control, and research. The study's reliance on observational data rather than detailed statistical or experimental methods limits the strength of its evidence, but it provides important insights into the operational and logistical complexities of managing chikungunya outbreaks. These findings have implications for improving public health readiness in regions at risk of similar arboviral epidemics, particularly in Europe and beyond.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为制定应对未来基孔肯雅热暴发的整合性应对策略提供了信息,特别是在流行病学特征相似的地区。

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
papers.abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, addressing the need for rapid, portable, and accurate methods to track viral diversity and evolution during outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the principles and application of nanopore sequencing for Chikungunya virus, examining its use in clinical and vector samples to recover complete genomes and monitor viral spread.
analysis.methods: Nanopore sequencing was used to directly sequence RNA and DNA by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling real-time, single-molecule analysis of Chikungunya virus genomes without the need for culture.
analysis.main_results: The method demonstrated the ability to rapidly recover full viral genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread during outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where nanopore sequencing provides a flexible and powerful tool for monitoring Chikungunya virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective genomic surveillance strategies for Chikungunya virus, enhancing outbreak response and epidemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges challenges in basecalling and error correction but highlights robust quality control pipelines that ensure reliable results, supporting a moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the application of nanopore sequencing in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomics, emphasizing its advantages in real-time, portable, and long-read analysis. The research highlights how nanopore sequencing enables rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity and spread. The authors interpret these findings as a significant advancement in pathogen surveillance, particularly for resource-limited settings, where the method offers flexibility and power. The study notes challenges in basecalling and error correction but underscores the reliability of quality control pipelines. These results have implications for improving genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness for CHIKV. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the acknowledged limitations in the sequencing process, though the method's potential is well-supported by prior experiences with other pathogens.

papers.title_zh: 纳米孔测序用于基孔肯雅病毒:原理与应用。
papers.source_body_en: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

papers.title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides an overview of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemiology, biology, and pathogenesis. It describes the virus as an arthropod-borne alphavirus transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, causing acute febrile illness with severe polyarthralgia and potential chronic complications. The virus has a spherical, enveloped virion with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry and a positive-sense RNA genome encoding replication and structural proteins. CHIKV replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving genomic and subgenomic RNA synthesis, glycoprotein maturation, and budding at the plasma membrane. Since its introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence has remained high, with over 180,000 confirmed cases in 2025. The study highlights the expansion of CHIKV beyond Africa and Asia, driven by adaptive mutations that enhance transmission. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination, with VLP-based vaccines showing promise and live-attenuated formulations facing safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist, and current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. The evidence is general and does not include specific limitations or evidence strength assessments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种属于Togaviridae科的虫媒α病毒,主要通过埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)和白纹伊蚊(Aedes albopictus)传播。该病毒引起一种急性发热性疾病,特征为严重的、常为双侧性关节痛,可能进展为慢性肌肉骨骼疼痛,并偶有涉及心血管和神经系统系统的全身并发症。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究概述了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的结构、生物学及系统发育。研究内容包括病毒的结构、复制机制及其全球传播情况。分析涵盖了CHIKV谱系及其相关疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)具有球形、包膜的病毒颗粒(约70 nm),呈T = 4二十面体对称结构,包含介导受体结合和膜融合的E1/E2糖蛋白异二聚体。其正链RNA基因组(约11.8 kb)编码用于复制的非结构蛋白和用于病毒颗粒组装的结构蛋白。病毒复制发生在细胞质囊泡中,涉及基因组和亚基因组RNA的合成,随后是糖蛋白成熟和在细胞膜上出芽。
elements_zh.main_results: 自2013年引入美洲以来,全球发病率仍保持较高水平,2025年报告了超过180,000例确诊病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 从流行病学角度看,CHIKV已扩展至非洲和亚洲以外的地区,其主要传播模式由适应性进化增强其传播能力。预防策略依赖于媒介控制和疫苗接种;基于病毒样颗粒(VLP)的疫苗(如Vimkunya)显示出前景,而减毒活疫苗则面临安全性问题。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物;现有管理措施为支持性治疗,但针对病毒复制和免疫调节的试验性疗法正在研发中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

papers.title_zh: 从野外采集的蚊虫中检测和测序基孔肯雅病毒的方案。
papers.source_body_en: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

papers.title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
papers.abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

full_text_sections.abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed a dataset of CHIKV sequences collected across different regions, hosts, and epidemic periods to characterize evolutionary pressures on the E2 glycoprotein.
analysis.methods: The researchers used diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to assess genetic variation and evolutionary dynamics, and performed spatial–temporal stratification and Fixation index (Fst) analysis to evaluate population structure.
analysis.main_results: Nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period (Pi = 0.085) and decreased in more recent outbreak periods (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests showed signs of both purifying and positive selection across lineages, with specific codons identified as sites of diversifying signals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein, revealing lineage-specific adaptations that may influence immune evasion and viral fitness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the genetic evolution of CHIKV, which can inform surveillance strategies, vaccine development, and understanding of viral adaptation during outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on sequence data, which may not capture all evolutionary pressures. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on computational and statistical analyses of genetic variation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host interaction and immune evasion. Using a dataset of sequences from various regions and time periods, the researchers applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures. Results showed that nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period and decreased in recent outbreaks. Neutrality tests indicated both purifying and positive selection across CHIKV lineages, with specific codons identified as sites of diversifying signals. These findings suggest that the E2 glycoprotein undergoes lineage-specific adaptations, which may impact viral fitness and immune evasion. The study provides valuable insights for understanding CHIKV evolution and its implications for public health, though it is limited by its reliance on sequence data and computational methods. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on statistical and analytical approaches to genetic variation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)中E2糖蛋白的遗传多样性及进化,重点关注其在宿主细胞附着、免疫识别和谱系分化中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了不同地区、宿主以及流行病时期的CHIKV序列数据集,以表征E2糖蛋白上的进化压力。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用多样性指数、中性检验和单倍型网络分析来评估遗传变异和进化动态,并进行了时空分层分析和固定指数(Fst)分析以评估种群结构。
elements_zh.main_results: 核苷酸多样性在扩张前时期(Pi = 0.085)最高,而在近期的暴发时期则显著降低(Pi = 0.012)。中性检验显示在谱系中存在纯化选择和正向选择的信号,并确定了特定密码子作为分化信号的位点。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突出了CHIKV E2糖蛋白的时空进化特性,揭示了可能影响免疫逃逸和病毒适应性的谱系特异性适应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为了解CHIKV的遗传进化提供了见解,有助于制定监测策略、疫苗开发以及理解病毒在暴发期间的适应过程。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于序列数据,可能无法全面捕捉所有进化压力。证据强度中等,因为它是基于遗传变异的计算和统计分析。

papers.title: Severe chikungunya infection requiring intensive care unit admission during the 2024– 2025 outbreak on Réunion Island: a multicentre observational study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Chikungunya (CHIK) is an arboviral disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Following the 2005–2006 outbreak, Réunion Island experienced a new outbreak in 2024–2025, with more than 54,500 laboratory-confirmed cases. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, severe manifestations, and outcomes of CHIK and to identify factors associated with mortality among patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission for severe disease. This multicentre observational study was conducted in the three adult ICUs on Réunion Island. All patients aged ≥ 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CHIK infection who were admitted between 23 August 2024 and 24 June 2025 were evaluated. Among 55,545 laboratory-confirmed cases, 554 patients required hospitalisation and 44 patients with severe CHIK required ICU admission. Median age was 69 years, and 91% of patients had at least one comorbidity. The main organ failures were renal (59%), circulatory (43%), respiratory (41%), and neurological (14%). Half of the patients received catecholamines, 32% required invasive mechanical ventilation, and 30% underwent renal replacement therapy. In-hospital mortality was 29%. Pre-existing diabetes mellitus was the only independent predictor of mortality (OR 4.92, 95% CI 1.02–23.81; P = 0.047). Severe CHIK can cause life-threatening multiorgan involvement, particularly in older patients with comorbidities. Hepatorenal involvement predominated, although neurological, cardiac, and haemorrhagic manifestations similar to those reported with other arboviral infections were also observed. These findings highlight the need for close monitoring of vulnerable patients, particularly those with diabetes, as well as effective preventive measures to mitigate the risk of future outbreaks.

The background highlights the need for understanding severe CHIK manifestations, especially in vulnerable populations, given the 2024–2025 outbreak on Réunion Island with over 54,500 laboratory-confirmed cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicentre observational study was conducted in the three adult ICUs on Réunion Island, evaluating all patients aged ≥ 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CHIK infection who were admitted between 23 August 2024 and 24 June 2025. Among 55,545 laboratory-confirmed cases, 44 patients required ICU admission.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated clinical characteristics, severe manifestations, and outcomes of CHIK infection, including organ failures, treatments received, and in-hospital mortality. Pre-existing diabetes mellitus was identified as the only independent predictor of mortality.
analysis.main_results: The study found that the median age of patients was 69 years, with 91% having at least one comorbidity. The main organ failures were renal (59%), circulatory (43%), respiratory (41%), and neurological (14%). Half of the patients received catecholamines, 32% required invasive mechanical ventilation, and 30% underwent renal replacement therapy. In-hospital mortality was 29%, with pre-existing diabetes mellitus being the only independent predictor of mortality (OR 4.92, 95% CI 1.02–23.81; P = 0.047).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the need for close monitoring of vulnerable patients, particularly those with diabetes, as well as effective preventive measures to mitigate the risk of future outbreaks. The study identified pre-existing diabetes mellitus as the only independent predictor of mortality, which is a novel finding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for severe CHIK infection, particularly in older patients with comorbidities. They also emphasize the importance of monitoring and managing diabetes in patients with CHIK infection to improve outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and the potential for confounding factors. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述基孔肯雅热(CHIK)感染的临床特征、严重表现和结局,特别是针对需要进入重症监护病房(ICU)的患者,以识别与暴发相关的因素。背景强调了了解严重CHIK表现的重要性,尤其是在易感人群中,鉴于2024–2025年留尼汪岛的暴发,实验室确诊病例超过54,500例。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在留尼汪岛的三个成人ICU中进行,评估了所有年龄≥18岁、实验室确诊基孔肯雅热感染并在2024年8月23日至2025年6月24日期间入院的患者。在55,545例实验室确诊病例中,有44例患者需要进入ICU。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究评估了基孔肯雅热感染的临床特征、严重表现和结局,包括器官衰竭情况、接受的治疗以及院内死亡率。既往糖尿病被确定为唯一独立预测院内死亡率的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: The study found that the median age of patients was 69 years, with 91% having at least one comorbidity. The main organ failures were renal (59%), circulatory (43%), respiratory (41%), and neurological (14%). Half of the patients received catecholamines, 32% required invasive mechanical ventilation, and 30% underwent renal replacement therapy. In-hospital mortality was 29%, with pre-existing diabetes mellitus being the only independent predictor of mortality (OR 4.92, 95% CI 1.02–23.81; P = 0.047).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现强调了对易感患者,特别是糖尿病患者进行密切监测的必要性,以及采取有效预防措施以降低未来暴发风险的重要性。本研究确定既往糖尿病是唯一独立预测院内死亡率的因素,这是一个新的发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为严重基孔肯雅热感染的监测、管理及治疗策略提供信息,特别是在有合并症的老年患者中。它们还强调了在基孔肯雅热感染患者中监测和管理糖尿病的重要性,以改善预后。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其观察性设计以及可能存在混杂因素。样本量适中,研究结果可能无法推广到其他人群。本研究为既往糖尿病与严重基孔肯雅热感染中院内死亡率之间的关联提供了中等证据。

analysis_zh.methods: 本研究评估了基孔肯雅热感染的临床特征、严重表现和结局,包括器官衰竭情况、接受的治疗以及院内死亡率。既往糖尿病被确定为唯一独立预测院内死亡率的因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现强调了对易感患者,特别是糖尿病患者进行密切监测的必要性,以及采取有效预防措施以降低未来暴发风险的重要性。本研究确定既往糖尿病是唯一独立预测院内死亡率的因素,这是一个新的发现。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为严重基孔肯雅热感染的监测、管理及治疗策略提供信息,特别是在有合并症的老年患者中。它们还强调了在基孔肯雅热感染患者中监测和管理糖尿病的重要性,以改善预后。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其观察性设计以及可能存在混杂因素。样本量适中,研究结果可能无法推广到其他人群。本研究为既往糖尿病与严重基孔肯雅热感染中院内死亡率之间的关联提供了中等证据。

papers.title: Workflow for Long-Read Amplicon Sequencing of Chikungunya Virus Using Oxford Nanopore Technology.
papers.abstract: This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在使用 Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) 平台开发可靠的 基因组 (CHIKV) 全 基因组 测序工作流程,满足处理 基因组监测 中低至中等病毒载量的改进方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了样品处理、病毒 RNA 提取、质量控制、cDNA 合成、多重 PCR 扩增、文库制备、测序和初级生物信息处理的分步方案,但没有提及特定人群或样本量。
elements_zh.methods: 该程序包括样品处理、病毒 RNA 提取、质量控制、cDNA 合成、多重 PCR 扩增、文库制备、测序和初级生物信息处理的详细说明。
elements_zh.main_results: 该协议的开发是为了最大限度地提高实验室的重现性,适用于 基因组监测 应用,包括 暴发 调查和分子 流行病学,即使在处理低至中等病毒载量时也是如此。

papers.title: Optimized Amplicon Strategy for Long-Read Sequencing of the Chikungunya Virus Genome.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

papers.title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

papers.title: Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test Against Chikungunya Virus Using Liver Homogenate.
papers.abstract: We adapted the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates instead of serum. This approach enables serological investigation using tissues collected from animal carcasses as nonhuman primate ones, during arbovirus surveillance, expanding opportunities for CHIKV monitoring and strengthening epidemiological surveillance efforts.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a novel method for detecting chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies using liver homogenates, addressing the need for alternative serological approaches in arbovirus surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved adapting the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to use liver homogenates instead of serum, focusing on nonhuman primate tissues collected during arbovirus surveillance.
analysis.methods: The plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) was modified to utilize liver homogenates as the medium for detecting CHIKV neutralizing antibodies, replacing the traditional serum-based approach.
analysis.main_results: The adapted PRNT method successfully detected CHIKV neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates, demonstrating its feasibility for serological investigation in nonhuman primate tissues.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This adaptation provides a new tool for CHIKV monitoring, particularly in scenarios where serum samples are not available, and highlights the potential of using alternative biological matrices in virological studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer a methodological advancement for arbovirus surveillance, enabling more comprehensive monitoring of CHIKV in nonhuman primate tissues and supporting improved epidemiological data collection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to demonstrating the feasibility of the method in nonhuman primate tissues, with no reported statistical analysis or broader validation, resulting in moderate confidence in its application.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an adaptation of the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates rather than serum. The research was motivated by the need for alternative serological methods in arbovirus surveillance, particularly when serum samples are unavailable. The modified PRNT successfully identified CHIKV neutralizing antibodies in nonhuman primate tissues, offering a new approach for CHIKV monitoring. This method could enhance epidemiological surveillance efforts by utilizing tissues from animal carcasses. However, the study lacks statistical analysis and broader validation, limiting the confidence in its application. The findings are significant for improving surveillance strategies but require further testing to establish their reliability in diverse contexts.

papers.title: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Analysis of Ligand Binding Kinetics in Chikungunya Virus Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

papers.title: RT-RPA-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

papers.title_zh: 基于 RT-RPA 辅助 CRISPR/Cas12a 的 基孔肯雅病毒 等温检测。
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

papers.title: Production of Viral Particles from a Chikungunya Virus Infectious Clone.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection.

papers.title: Cross-protection of wildtype and vaccine-derived chikungunya virus antibodies against chikungunya and Mayaro viruses in mice
papers.abstract: Abstract The live-attenuated vaccine IXCHIQ against chikungunya virus (CHIKV) was approved in 2023, with its efficacy evaluated using human neutralizing antibody titers as surrogate effectiveness criterion. Previous in vivo studies assessed its efficacy at high CHIKV-specific antibody titers, whereas its efficacy and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) risks at suboptimal levels mimicking long-term immunity remain poorly characterized. Here, we assessed antibody-mediated protection following vaccination or natural infection by passively immunizing transiently immunocompromised mice with graded doses of pooled immune sera before challenge with two CHIKV genotypes or the related Mayaro virus (MAYV). Protection was evaluated using viral loads at 3 days post-infection and clinical parameters. Vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies conferred strong protection against both CHIKV genotypes, even at antibody concentrations nearing ELISA detection limits. In contrast, protection against MAYV required higher titers. Our findings align with previous studies supporting durable protection against CHIKV and partial cross-protection against MAYV.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the understanding of antibody-mediated protection against CHIKV and may guide vaccine development and cross-protection strategies against related viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cross-protection of antibodies against chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and the related Mayaro virus (MAYV) in mice. The live-attenuated vaccine IXCHIQ was evaluated for its efficacy using human neutralizing antibody titers as a surrogate effectiveness criterion. The research aimed to assess antibody-mediated protection following vaccination or natural infection by passively immunizing transiently immunocompromised mice with graded doses of pooled immune sera before challenge with two CHIKV genotypes or MAYV. The results showed that vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies conferred strong protection against both CHIKV genotypes, even at antibody concentrations nearing ELISA detection limits, while protection against MAYV required higher titers. These findings align with previous studies supporting durable protection against CHIKV and partial cross-protection against MAYV. The study's significance lies in its contribution to understanding antibody-mediated immunity against CHIKV and its implications for vaccine development. However, the study is limited to in vivo mouse models, which may not fully reflect human immune responses, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the reliance on surrogate markers.

papers.title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) poses a growing global health threat, prompting the development of a rapid detection method. Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. By offering a point-of-care, visual LAMP assay, the protocol has the potential to enhance CHIKV surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. No limitations or evidence strength assessments were reported in the abstract.

papers.title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

papers.title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
papers.abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

The protocol involves expressing the protein at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purifying it under native conditions using immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The method typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, which has been successfully used for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening. The described procedure offers a reliable approach for studying CHIKV protease function, potentially aiding in the development of antiviral therapies and diagnostics. However, the study is limited to methodological description and does not provide clinical or epidemiological data, which limits its direct public health implications. The evidence is strong for the method's effectiveness in producing active nsP2pro but lacks broader application details.

papers.source_body_en: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

papers.title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
papers.abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

papers.title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

papers.title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
papers.abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. papers.title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
papers.abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

papers.source_body_en: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

papers.title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
papers.abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

papers.title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes the epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas, focusing on the spread and burden of these diseases. The review included 15 studies from PubMed and SciELO between 2012 and 2025. Key findings indicate that dengue incidence has increased globally since 1990, with significant regional variations and a high burden in Latin America. Chikungunya expanded across the Americas since 2013, causing explosive urban outbreaks and persistent joint manifestations. Urbanization, the spread of Aedes species, and insecticide resistance are identified as factors that facilitate transmission. The review highlights the need for new vaccines and integrated vector control strategies to address the growing public health challenge posed by these arboviruses in tropical and subtropical cities.

papers.source_body_en: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

papers.title: Clinical and virological characterisation of Oropouche, dengue, and chikungunya during simultaneous co-circulation in the State of Espírito Santo, Brazil: a retrospective observational study
papers.abstract: Background Dengue (DENV), chikungunya (CHIKV), and Oropouche (OROV) viruses co-circulate in Brazil and present with overlapping acute febrile syndromes, complicating clinical differentiation. Comparative data integrating clinical phenotyping and viral load dynamics across these arboviruses are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study using linked surveillance and laboratory databases from Espírito Santo State, Brazil (2024–2025). We aimed to compare DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections and to explore their virological correlates. Cycle threshold (Ct) values, used as a relative semi-quantitative proxy for viral RNA levels, were analysed within each virus to characterise temporal dynamics and clinical expression. Multinomial logistic regression identified clinical features associated with arboviral infection; associations between Ct values and clinical domain scores were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. Findings Among 10,793 cases (4058 DENV, 2508 CHIKV, 4227 OROV), Oropouche affected older individuals (median age 49 years, interquartile range [IQR] 43–56) and was characterised by near-universal fever (97·8%), headache (96·2%), and intense arthralgia (86·4%), with fewer gastrointestinal and mucocutaneous manifestations. After adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset, increased odds of arthritis (OR 5·22, 95% CI 4·08–6·68) and rash (OR 2·39, 95% CI 1·83–3·12) were observed for CHIKV versus OROV. Conversely, nausea (OR 2·98, 95% CI 2·52–3·53), vomiting (OR 2·54, 95% CI 2·01–3·21), and retro-orbital pain (OR 8·00, 95% CI 6·69–9·56) were positively associated with DENV versus OROV. Dengue and chikungunya showed progressive Ct increases over time, consistent with viral decay. Oropouche displayed a non-monotonic, with lower Ct values and higher systemic and musculoskeletal domain scores after adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. Interpretation The distinct clinical and temporal patterns identified provide descriptive foundations that may inform future development of diagnostic algorithms and sampling strategies, pending formal predictive validation. Funding This study was partially funded by the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa e Inovação do Espírito Santo (FAPES), with additional institutional support from the Brazilian Ministry of Health and the Government of the State of Espírito Santo.

papers.source_body_en: Background Dengue (DENV), chikungunya (CHIKV), and Oropouche (OROV) viruses co-circulate in Brazil and present with overlapping acute febrile syndromes, complicating clinical differentiation. Comparative data integrating clinical phenotyping and viral load dynamics across these arboviruses are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study using linked surveillance and laboratory databases from Espírito Santo State, Brazil (2024–2025). We aimed to compare DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections and to explore their virological correlates. Cycle threshold (Ct) values, used as a relative semi-quantitative proxy for viral RNA levels, were analysed within each virus to characterise temporal dynamics and clinical expression. Multinomial logistic regression identified clinical features associated with arboviral infection; associations between Ct values and clinical domain scores were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. Findings Among 10,793 cases (4058 DENV, 2508 CHIKV, 4227 OROV), Oropouche affected older individuals (median age 49 years, interquartile range [IQR] 43–56) and was characterised by near-universal fever (97·8%), headache (96·2%), and intense arthralgia (86·4%), with fewer gastrointestinal and mucocutaneous manifestations. After adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset, increased odds of arthritis (OR 5·22, 95% CI 4·08–6·68) and rash (OR 2·39, 95% CI 1·83–3·12) were observed for CHIKV versus OROV. Conversely, nausea (OR 2·98, 95% CI 2·52–3·53), vomiting (OR 2·54, 95% CI 2·01–3·21), and retro-orbital pain (OR 8·00, 95% CI 6·69–9·56) were positively associated with DENV versus OROV. Dengue and chikungunya showed progressive Ct increases over time, consistent with viral decay. Oropouche displayed a non-monotonic, with lower Ct values and higher systemic and musculoskeletal domain scores after adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. Interpretation The distinct clinical and temporal patterns identified provide descriptive foundations that may inform future development of diagnostic algorithms and sampling strategies, pending formal predictive validation. Funding This study was partially funded by the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa e Inovação do Espírito Santo (FAPES), with additional institutional support from the Brazilian Ministry of Health and the Government of the State of Espírito Santo.

papers.title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
papers.abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

papers.abstract_zh: 疟疾和基孔肯雅热的混合感染是一种罕见的表现,对诊断提出了挑战,特别是因为两种感染都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。我们介绍了一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者,无既往病史,有 7 天发热、头晕、全身无力、关节痛 和呕吐病史。入院时,她出现发热、心动过速和低血压,对晶体液初始复苏的血流动力学反应不足,需要血管加压药支持。高级心血管评估显示主要是血管舒张和高动力特征,其特征是高心输出量、降低的全身血管阻力和保留的每搏输出量。左心室和右心室收缩和舒张功能仍然保留,具有足够的 TAPSE 和 MAPSE,并且没有明显的心室扩张或局部收缩力异常。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。研究显示严重贫血,血红蛋白水平为 6 g/dL,并且肝脾肿大。厚厚的血涂片鉴定出疟原虫。该患者的间日疟检测呈阳性,而基孔肯雅热PCR检测呈阳性,登革热检测呈阴性,证实了双重感染。开始静脉注射青蒿琥酯,随后使用蒿甲醚-本芴醇,此外还进行血管活性支持和输注两个单位的浓缩红细胞。患者的血流动力学逐渐恢复,临床病程良好。该病例强调了考虑 媒介 传播的合并感染和表征血流动力学表型以区分血管舒张性休克和心源性损害的重要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在强调间日疟原虫和 基孔肯雅病毒 合并感染带来的诊断挑战,特别是在区分其全身表现和血流动力学影响方面。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 病例报告 对一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者进行,该患者无既往病史,表现为发烧、头晕、全身无力、病例报告 和呕吐。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过 基孔肯雅病毒 的 PCR 检测和间日疟原虫的厚血涂片分析以及临床和血流动力学评估,确认了患者的双重感染。
analysis_zh.main_results: 心血管评估显示高动力特征,心输出量高,全身血管阻力降低,每搏输出量保持不变,但没有发现心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,间日疟原虫和 基孔肯雅病毒 的共同感染可导致复杂的血流动力学变化,需要与其他休克原因仔细区分。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在发热性疾病中识别 媒介 传播的合并感染的重要性,并强调了在临床环境中准确表征血流动力学特征的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个病例报告,可能无法推广。然而,鉴于详细的临床和诊断结果,证据是强有力的。

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTBackground: Arboviruses in hospital environments may represent a neglected risk of nosocomial infections. This study investigated arboviruses in Aedes spp. larvae collected from a hospital area in Brasília, Federal District, Brazil. Methods: Eighteen ovitraps were deployed for 26 weeks. Hatched Aedes spp. larvae were pooled weekly, and viral detection was performed by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR. Results: Dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, and 4, Zika virus, and Chikungunya virus were identified, with an overall positivity rate of 30.76%. Conclusion: The surveillance strategy effectively detected arboviral RNA in a hospital setting, suggesting local arboviral circulation associated with the transmission triad.Keywords: Ovitrap, RT-qPCR, One Health, Epidemiological monitoring, Entomo-virological surveillance SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIALSupplementary Material Table 1 Supplementary MaterialsSupplementary Material Table 1 ACKNOWLEDGMENTSWe offer our deepest thanks to the Armed Forces Hospital that provided technical support for the development and implementation of this study. papers.title_original: Molecular Detection of Arboviruses in Aedes spp. Larvae During Entomo-Virological Surveillance in a Hospital Area of Brasília, Federal District, Brazil

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the presence of arboviruses, including Chikungunya virus, in Aedes spp. larvae within a hospital area to identify potential risks of nosocomial infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed entomo-virological surveillance using ovitraps deployed for 26 weeks in a hospital area of Brasília, Federal District, Brazil, to collect Aedes spp.
analysis.methods: Larvae were pooled weekly and viral detection was conducted using reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to identify arboviruses such as Dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya viruses.
analysis.main_results: Chikungunya virus was identified among the arboviruses, with an overall positivity rate of 30.76% for Dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, and 4, Zika virus, and Chikungunya virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the hospital area is a site of local arboviral circulation, highlighting the importance of entomo-virological surveillance in detecting early transmission hotspots.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for integrated surveillance strategies to monitor arboviral activity in healthcare settings, aiding in the prevention of nosocomial infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on ovitraps and RT-qPCR may limit the comprehensiveness of viral detection, but the evidence is moderate due to the direct observation of arboviral RNA in larvae.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted entomo-virological surveillance in a hospital area of Brasília, Brazil, using ovitraps to collect Aedes spp. larvae over 26 weeks. Viral detection was performed via RT-qPCR, revealing the presence of Dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, and 4, Zika virus, and Chikungunya virus, with an overall positivity rate of 30.76%. The surveillance strategy effectively identified arboviral RNA in the hospital setting, suggesting local circulation associated with the transmission triad. These findings emphasize the value of entomo-virological approaches in detecting early arbovirus transmission and highlight the need for targeted surveillance in healthcare environments. However, the study's reliance on ovitraps and RT-qPCR may limit the scope of detection, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the direct observation of viral RNA without further causal analysis.

papers.title: Entomological investigations into yellow fever outbreak in northern Ghana.
papers.abstract: Arboviruses are pathogens of emerging/re-emerging infectious diseases. Half the world's population is at risk. Recent African epidemics confirmed 19,569 cases with 820 deaths. In Ghana, Savannah Region had yellow fever (YF) outbreak in 2021. Reports revealed 35 deaths, 202 suspected cases (case fatality rate (CFR) = 17%), and 70 confirmed cases (CFR = 50%). This paper presents YF outbreak entomological investigations findings. A team with expertise in YF outbreak response were assembled and tasked to assess, contain and/or control the rapid spread of YF. Immature Aedes aegypti were collected in/around houses, and adult sampled using BG-Sentinel traps, oral aspirators and Prokopack. The chikungunya, dengue fever, YF, and Zika viruses screening using real time reverse-transcription PCR (detection limit <10 RNA copies/reaction) followed mosquitoes morphological identification. Breeding containers (12,264) were examined. Larvae (3,885) and pupae (1,186) were obtained from 173 containers (positivity rate = 1.26%). Larvae were identified with short and stout siphons. Pupae had short but distinct serrated spicules on paddle fringe and branched/fanlike (6-7 branches) seta 9-VIII. Out of 1,001 houses surveyed, 130 were positive for larvae/pupae (positivity rate = 12.99%). Receptacles included plastic [46.95% (6,529)], metallic [43.32% (6,024)], clay jar [5.42% (753)], tire [4.06% (565)], and well [0.24% (34)]. WHO larval indices thresholds (BI, CI, HI, and PDI) were used to assess risk. Exactly 1,571 adults were identified [Aedes aegypti aegypti (35), Aedes aegypti formosus (619), and Culex sp. Outdoor collection were higher (86.4%) than indoors (13.6%). No arboviruses were detected. Generally, vector indices/densities suggested high-risk arbovirus transmission although vectors were not arbovirus positive. Aedes aegypti formosus was dominant. They are bridge vectors maintaining sylvatic YF cycles and spillover transmission. High risk for YF poses public health threat that calls for Aedes mosquito surveillance systems and vector control strategies. formosus might be drivers for outbreak and/or YF transmission.
